__inputs.name: DS_CASH_FLOW_COMMANDER
__inputs.label: Cash Flow Commander Postgres
__inputs.description: Postgres datasource pointed at the apps database, connecting as grafana_ro. Set the datasource's default schema to cash_flow_commander, or leave it — every query here is schema-qualified.

description: What the solar panels are worth each billing period, and what net metering hides. With no battery, solar consumed on site never crosses the meter, so the bill understates both gross generation and true household consumption by that amount.

panels.title: What the panels were worth, per billing period
panels.description: Avoided cost = solar you consumed on site, priced at that bill's marginal retail rate (contract energy rate + per-kWh TDU delivery, grossed up by the bill's effective tax rate). Fixed charges are excluded — solar does not avoid them. Buyback credit is the actual credit line on the bill, not a model. Bars are plotted at the start of each billing period.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bill_rates AS (
  SELECT b.invoice_number, b.service_start, b.service_end, b.total_kwh,
         b.total_current_charges,
         MAX(li.rate_cents_kwh) FILTER (WHERE li.category = 'energy') AS energy_rate_cents,
         COALESCE(SUM(li.amount) FILTER (
           WHERE li.category = 'delivery'
             AND (li.description ILIKE '%per kWh%' OR li.description ILIKE '%- Energy%')
         ), 0) AS delivery_variable,
         COALESCE(SUM(li.amount) FILTER (WHERE li.category = 'tax'), 0) AS taxes,
         COALESCE(-SUM(li.amount) FILTER (WHERE li.category = 'credit'), 0) AS buyback_credit
  FROM cash_flow_commander.bills b
  JOIN cash_flow_commander.bill_line_items li USING (invoice_number)
  WHERE b.service_start IS NOT NULL AND b.total_kwh > 0
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
),
marginal AS (
  SELECT *,
         (COALESCE(energy_rate_cents, 0) + 100.0 * delivery_variable / total_kwh)
           * (1 + taxes / NULLIF(total_current_charges - taxes, 0)) / 100.0
           AS marginal_rate
  FROM bill_rates
  WHERE energy_rate_cents IS NOT NULL
),
usage AS (
  SELECT m.invoice_number,
         SUM(u.value) FILTER (WHERE u.metric = 'production')  AS production,
         SUM(u.value) FILTER (WHERE u.metric = 'generation')  AS exported,
         SUM(u.value) FILTER (WHERE u.metric = 'consumption') AS imported
  FROM marginal m
  JOIN cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals u
    ON u.granularity = '15min'
   AND timezone('America/Chicago', u.ts)::date BETWEEN m.service_start AND m.service_end
  GROUP BY 1
),
value AS (
  SELECT m.service_start, m.service_end, m.marginal_rate, m.buyback_credit,
         m.total_current_charges,
         u.production, u.exported, u.imported,
         u.production - u.exported AS self_consumed,
         (u.production - u.exported) * m.marginal_rate AS avoided_cost
  FROM marginal m
  JOIN usage u USING (invoice_number)
  WHERE u.production IS NOT NULL AND u.exported IS NOT NULL AND u.imported IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT service_start::timestamptz AS time,
       avoided_cost   AS "Avoided cost (self-consumed)",
       buyback_credit AS "Buyback credit (exported)",
       total_current_charges AS "Bill actually paid"
FROM value
WHERE true AND $__timeFilter(service_start::timestamptz)
ORDER BY service_start

panels.description: Avoided cost plus buyback credit, summed over every billing period in range.

panels.title: Where the value comes from
panels.description: Self-consumption is worth far more per kWh than export: you avoid the full retail rate including delivery and tax, while exported kWh earn only the buyback rate.

panels.title: Solar % of consumption — monthly
panels.description: Total solar production divided by total household consumption for the month. Consumption = metered import + self-consumed solar. Above 100% means the panels produced more than the house used that month. Months missing metered import/export are omitted rather than scored.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bucketed AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', timezone('America/Chicago', ts)) AS bucket,
         SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'production')  AS production,
         SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'generation')  AS exported,
         SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'consumption') AS imported
  FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
  WHERE granularity = '15min'
    AND metric IN ('production', 'generation', 'consumption')
    AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY 1
),
scored AS (
  SELECT bucket,
         production,
         imported + (production - exported) AS consumption
  FROM bucketed
  WHERE production IS NOT NULL AND exported IS NOT NULL AND imported IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT bucket AS time,
       100.0 * production / NULLIF(consumption, 0) AS "Solar % of consumption"
FROM scored
ORDER BY bucket

panels.title: Solar % of consumption — daily
panels.description: Same ratio per local day. Daily values swing hard with weather and load, so a 7-day trailing average is overlaid. Days above 100% are days the panels out-produced the house.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bucketed AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('day', timezone('America/Chicago', ts)) AS bucket,
         SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'production')  AS production,
         SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'generation')  AS exported,
         SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'consumption') AS imported
  FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
  WHERE granularity = '15min'
    AND metric IN ('production', 'generation', 'consumption')
    AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY 1
),
scored AS (
  SELECT bucket,
         production,
         imported + (production - exported) AS consumption
  FROM bucketed
  WHERE production IS NOT NULL AND exported IS NOT NULL AND imported IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT bucket AS time,
       100.0 * production / NULLIF(consumption, 0) AS "Solar % of consumption",
       AVG(100.0 * production / NULLIF(consumption, 0))
         OVER (ORDER BY bucket ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
         AS "7-day average"
FROM scored
ORDER BY bucket

options.content:
**Solar % of consumption** = total production ÷ total consumption, per bucket. Consumption is what the house actually used: metered grid import **plus** the solar that never crossed the meter. It can exceed 100% when the panels out-produce the house — that surplus is exported.

**What the panels are worth** = *avoided cost* (solar consumed on site, priced at the marginal retail rate you would otherwise have paid) + *buyback credit* (the actual credit line on the bill for exported kWh).

**self_consumption = gross_production − exported**  ·  **true_consumption = imported + self_consumption**

`production` is gross AC output at the inverters (Enphase). `consumption` is metered grid import — what you were billed for. `generation` is metered export. Solar used the instant it was made crosses no meter and appears in neither, which is why total consumption has to be reconstructed rather than read off the bill.

Marginal rate = contract energy rate + per-kWh TDU delivery, grossed up by the bill's effective tax rate; fixed charges excluded. Buckets use a literal `America/Chicago`; buckets missing metered import/export are omitted, never scored as zero.

panels.title: Monthly energy: billed vs hidden vs exported
panels.description: Stacked bars. 'Billed' is what the retailer charged you for. 'Self-consumed' is solar that never crossed the meter — invisible on the bill. Together they are what the house actually used.

targets.rawSql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', timezone('America/Chicago', ts)) AS month,
         metric,
         SUM(value) AS kwh
  FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
  WHERE granularity = '15min'
    AND metric IN ('production', 'consumption', 'generation')
    AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT month AS time,
       SUM(kwh) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'consumption') AS "Billed (grid import)",
       SUM(kwh) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'production')
         - SUM(kwh) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'generation') AS "Self-consumed solar (hidden from bill)",
       SUM(kwh) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'generation') AS "Exported (buyback)"
FROM monthly
GROUP BY month
HAVING SUM(kwh) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'production') IS NOT NULL
   AND SUM(kwh) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'generation') IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY month

panels.title: Solar % of consumption (range)
panels.description: Total production divided by total consumption across the whole selected range.

targets.rawSql:
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT metric, SUM(value) AS kwh
  FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
  WHERE granularity = '15min'
    AND metric IN ('production', 'consumption', 'generation')
    AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY metric
),
d AS (
  SELECT (SELECT kwh FROM totals WHERE metric = 'production')  AS production,
         (SELECT kwh FROM totals WHERE metric = 'consumption') AS imported,
         (SELECT kwh FROM totals WHERE metric = 'generation')  AS exported
)
SELECT 100.0 * production / NULLIF(imported + (production - exported), 0)
         AS "Solar % of consumption"
FROM d

panels.title: True consumption vs billed
panels.description: Left: what the house actually used. Right: what the retailer billed. The difference is self-consumed solar.

targets.rawSql:
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT metric, SUM(value) AS kwh
  FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
  WHERE granularity = '15min'
    AND metric IN ('production', 'consumption', 'generation')
    AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY metric
)
SELECT
  (SELECT kwh FROM totals WHERE metric = 'consumption') AS "Billed",
  (SELECT kwh FROM totals WHERE metric = 'consumption')
    + ((SELECT kwh FROM totals WHERE metric = 'production')
       - (SELECT kwh FROM totals WHERE metric = 'generation')) AS "True consumption"

panels.title: Daily flows: production, export, import
panels.description: Daily totals from the 15-minute series. Production above export is the self-consumed wedge.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date_trunc('day', timezone('America/Chicago', ts)) AS time,
       SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'production')  AS "Gross production",
       SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'generation')  AS "Exported",
       SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'consumption') AS "Imported (billed)"
FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
WHERE granularity = '15min'
  AND metric IN ('production', 'consumption', 'generation')
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Reconciliation by billing period
panels.description: Joins each bill's service period to the interval data. 'Billed kWh' is the figure on the bill; 'Metered import' is the summed interval data over the same period — they should agree closely. A large divergence means a coverage gap, not a billing error: check /coverage before trusting the row.

targets.rawSql:
WITH periods AS (
  SELECT service_start, service_end, total_kwh
  FROM cash_flow_commander.bills
  WHERE service_start IS NOT NULL AND service_end IS NOT NULL
),
per_period AS (
  SELECT p.service_start,
         p.service_end,
         p.total_kwh,
         SUM(u.value) FILTER (WHERE u.metric = 'production')  AS production,
         SUM(u.value) FILTER (WHERE u.metric = 'generation')  AS exported,
         SUM(u.value) FILTER (WHERE u.metric = 'consumption') AS imported
  FROM periods p
  JOIN cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals u
    ON u.granularity = '15min'
   AND timezone('America/Chicago', u.ts)::date BETWEEN p.service_start AND p.service_end
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
)
SELECT to_char(service_start, 'YYYY-MM-DD') || ' .. ' || to_char(service_end, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "Period",
       ROUND(total_kwh) AS "Billed kWh",
       ROUND(imported) AS "Metered import",
       ROUND(production) AS "Gross production",
       ROUND(exported) AS "Exported",
       ROUND(production - exported) AS "Self-consumed",
       ROUND(imported + (production - exported)) AS "True consumption",
       ROUND(100.0 * (production - exported) / NULLIF(imported + (production - exported), 0)) AS "Solar share %"
FROM per_period
WHERE production IS NOT NULL AND exported IS NOT NULL AND imported IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY service_start DESC

panels.title: Production only — renders without the electricity provider

options.content:
Everything above compares solar against the retailer's metered import/export, so a panel there goes blank for any day the electricity provider hasn't been captured yet — the line just ends early rather than gapping.

**These panels read `metric = 'production'` alone.** They stay current the moment an Enphase run lands, whether or not the retailer side has caught up, so a short line up top plus a current line down here means *the electricity data is behind*, not that solar stopped.

*Lifetime, per-year and freshness panels ignore the time picker on purpose.*

panels.title: Lifetime production
panels.description: All-time gross production at the inverters. Ignores the time picker.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT SUM(value) / 1000.0 AS "Lifetime production"
FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'

panels.title: Production in range
panels.description: Gross production summed over the selected time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT SUM(value) AS "Production in range"
FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)

panels.title: Average day in range
panels.description: Mean daily production across days in the selected range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT AVG(kwh) AS "Average day"
FROM (
  SELECT SUM(value) AS kwh
  FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
  WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'
    AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY date_trunc('day', timezone('America/Chicago', ts))
) x

panels.title: Best day in range
panels.description: Highest single-day production in the selected range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT MAX(kwh) AS "Best day"
FROM (
  SELECT SUM(value) AS kwh
  FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
  WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'
    AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY date_trunc('day', timezone('America/Chicago', ts))
) x

panels.title: Peak power in range
panels.description: Highest 15-minute average power. Interval kWh x 4 = kW sustained over that interval, so this is a 15-minute average and reads below true instantaneous peak.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT MAX(value) * 4 AS "Peak power"
FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)

panels.title: Days since last production
panels.description: Freshness of the Enphase feed, ignoring the time picker. 1 is normal (yesterday is the last complete day). Sustained 3+ means the gateway stopped reporting or a run is overdue.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT (CURRENT_DATE - MAX((timezone('America/Chicago', ts))::date))::int AS "Days since last production"
FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'

panels.title: Daily production
panels.description: Gross production per local day, from the 15-minute series. Depends on Enphase only, so this runs to the last captured day regardless of the electricity provider.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date_trunc('day', timezone('America/Chicago', ts)) AS time,
       SUM(value) AS "Daily production"
FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Monthly production
panels.description: Production per calendar month. The seasonal swing is the signal; compare the same month across years to see year-over-year drift.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', timezone('America/Chicago', ts)) AS time,
       SUM(value) AS "Monthly production"
FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Production by calendar year
panels.description: Annual totals across the whole series, ignoring the time picker. The first and last years are partial (system started mid-December 2021, and the current year is still running), so read only the complete years against each other when judging degradation.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT to_char(timezone('America/Chicago', ts), 'YYYY') AS "Year",
       SUM(value) / 1000.0 AS "Production (MWh)"
FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Average day shape, by hour
panels.description: Mean power for each hour of the day across the selected range, including nights as zero. A dented or lopsided curve points at shading or a string that stopped reporting.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT to_char(timezone('America/Chicago', ts), 'HH24') AS "Hour",
       AVG(value) * 4 AS "Average power"
FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Days well below their seasonal baseline
panels.description: Days that produced under half of the average of the 31-day window centred on them. The baseline moves with the season, so this is not just 'winter'. Most hits are weather; a run of them, or an isolated near-zero day in clear weather, is worth checking against Enlighten's per-panel view.

targets.rawSql:
WITH daily AS (
  SELECT (timezone('America/Chicago', ts))::date AS d,
         SUM(value) AS kwh
  FROM cash_flow_commander.usage_intervals
  WHERE granularity = '15min' AND metric = 'production'
    AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY 1
),
scored AS (
  SELECT d,
         kwh,
         AVG(kwh) OVER (ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN 15 PRECEDING AND 15 FOLLOWING) AS baseline
  FROM daily
)
SELECT to_char(d, 'YYYY-MM-DD')                  AS "Day",
       ROUND(kwh, 1)                             AS "Produced (kWh)",
       ROUND(baseline, 1)                        AS "Seasonal baseline (kWh)",
       ROUND(100.0 * kwh / NULLIF(baseline, 0))  AS "% of baseline"
FROM scored
WHERE baseline > 0
  AND kwh < 0.5 * baseline
ORDER BY d DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Cash Flow Commander — Solar & Net Metering
